title: Balanced plate sheet
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y3 lesson 5 (Balanced plate sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 5: Healthy eating: a balanced plate. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: The food groups
points: Protein: beans, eggs, fish, halal meat

panels.title: Sugary and fatty foods
points: Too much harms teeth and heart

box.title: Draw your dinner plate: about a third fruit and vegetables, about a third starchy food, then some protein and a little dairy

keywords.def: the right amount of each kind of food
foods that do a similar job, like fruit and vegetables

questions.q: Which food group is rice in?

questions.a: For example: beans, eggs, lentils, fish, halal chicken.

questions.q: Is a fizzy drink an every-day drink?
questions.a: No: water is best; fizzy drinks only sometimes.

questions.q: Core: Draw a balanced plate for your dinner with the right amounts of each group (pupil PDF).
questions.a: Half fruit and veg, starchy food, some protein, a little dairy.

questions.q: Extend: Write a menu for one healthy day: breakfast, lunch, dinner, a snack.
questions.a: A balanced day with fruit and vegetables at most meals.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why a plate of only chips is not tayyib for our body.
questions.a: It has too much fat and starch and no fruit, vegetables or protein.

questions.q: Which should be the biggest part of our plate?
questions.a: B) Fruit and vegetables. Fruit and vegetables are the largest part of a balanced plate.

questions.q: Halal and tayyib means food that is... A) allowed and good B) only tasty C) only sweet
Big question: could you be healthy eating only chips? Why?
questions.a: No: our body needs a balance of food groups.
